exercises.title: Logic gates and XOR
exercises.implementation:
Hand: truth tables, one perceptron weight update, and a 2D sketch showing why XOR has no linear separator.
Code: implement step activation and the update rule in NumPy; train on AND and OR, plot the boundaries. Try XOR and record failure.
exercises.deliverables: notes.md (worked update + XOR sketch); perceptron.py or .ipynb; predictions.csv; boundary.png.

exercises.title: Backprop by hand
exercises.implementation:
Hand: for XOR input (0,1)→1, use two hidden units, tanh activations, sigmoid output and binary cross-entropy to compute forward pass, gradients and one SGD update.
Code: train all four rows with manual NumPy backprop; repeat in PyTorch autograd and compare one gradient.
exercises.deliverables: notes.md or photographed workings; xor_numpy.py; xor_torch.py; loss_curve.png; four final predictions.

exercises.title: Recognize handwritten digits
exercises.implementation:
Hand: calculate one 3×3 convolution output, output shapes, and CNN versus MLP parameter counts.
Code: load MNIST with torchvision; train MLP and small LeNet-style nn.Module with DataLoader; evaluate held-out digits.
exercises.deliverables: digit_models.py; results.csv; two confusion matrices; 12 error images; notes.md on weight sharing and errors.

exercises.title: Tabular model comparison
exercises.implementation:
Hand: calculate one decision-tree split's impurity reduction and sketch a 2D SVM margin.
Code: use one fixed train/test split and scikit-learn Pipelines for tree, SVM, forest, boosting; add XGBoost if installed; tune on training data only.
exercises.deliverables: tabular_benchmark.py; metrics.csv; comparison plot; notes.md explaining leakage control and two error cases.

exercises.title: EM with hidden labels
exercises.implementation:
Hand: compute responsibilities and updated means for three points in a two-Gaussian mixture.
Code: generate a toy dataset; implement E and M steps in NumPy; plot likelihood and parameters over iterations and vary initialization.
exercises.deliverables: notes.md (one E/M iteration); em_numpy.py; trajectories.png; short initialization comparison.

exercises.title: Inspect the image benchmark
exercises.implementation:
Hand: write a one-page data card on labels, splits, and plausible leakage; use a small public image subset, not full ImageNet.
Code: inspect class counts and image dimensions, hash for duplicates, and create a reproducible train/validation split.
exercises.deliverables: data_card.md; audit.py; class_counts.csv; sample_grid.png; split manifest with random seed.

exercises.title: Trace a CNN
exercises.implementation:
Hand: trace tensor shapes and receptive fields for a small CNN; calculate one residual block's skip addition.
Code: implement a compact LeNet-style model in PyTorch and use hooks or a forward pass to check shapes; compare paper architectures in notes.
exercises.deliverables: architecture_notes.md; cnn_shapes.py; layer_shapes.csv; one feature-map figure.

exercises.title: Boxes versus masks
exercises.implementation:
Hand: calculate box IoU and mask IoU for one annotated example; explain semantic versus instance segmentation.
Code: annotate five images; run pretrained torchvision Mask R-CNN (SAM optional); compare predicted boxes/masks to your annotations.
exercises.deliverables: annotations/; detect_segment.py; five overlay images; iou.csv; notes.md comparing U-Net, Faster R-CNN, Mask R-CNN, SAM.

exercises.title: A* search
exercises.implementation:
Hand: trace open/closed sets and f=g+h for four A* expansions; test an inadmissible heuristic.
Code: write grid search with heapq, A* and uniform-cost modes; count expansions and verify optimal path costs.
exercises.deliverables: astar.py; small grid fixtures; paths.png; expansions.csv; handwritten trace in notes.md.

exercises.title: Belief-network inference
exercises.implementation:
Hand: draw a three-node belief network and calculate one posterior by enumerating hidden states.
Code: represent conditional-probability tables in NumPy and enumerate joint probabilities; compare computed posterior to your hand result.
exercises.deliverables: belief_network.py; cpts.csv; notes.md with graph, posterior calculation, and normalization check.

exercises.title: Learn a gridworld policy
exercises.implementation:
Hand: calculate one TD error and one Q-learning target from a transition.
Code: implement tabular Q-learning on deterministic FrozenLake; log episode rewards and learned Q table. Optional: small PyTorch DQN with replay/target net.
exercises.deliverables: notes.md (worked updates); q_learning.py; rewards.png; policy_grid.txt; optional dqn.py.

exercises.title: Mini AlphaZero self-play
exercises.implementation:
Hand: draw a tic-tac-toe search tree, calculate PUCT/UCB terms for one node, and normalize visit counts.
Code: implement rules, MCTS and self-play; use a tabular value/policy estimate first. Optional: replace it with a tiny PyTorch network.
exercises.deliverables: notes.md (one search); tictactoe_mcts.py; visit_targets.csv; win_draw_curves.png; optional network.py.

exercises.title: Plan with learned dynamics
exercises.implementation:
Hand: compare one true grid transition with a model-predicted transition and sketch planning in latent state.
Code: collect trajectories, fit a tiny transition predictor, plan using it, and compare resulting paths with known-rule planning.
exercises.deliverables: notes.md (MuZero diagram and model errors); dynamics.py; transitions.csv; planning_comparison.png.

exercises.title: Inspect word vectors
exercises.implementation:
Hand: form skip-gram input–target pairs and work one dot-product score for two word vectors.
Code: train a small embedding layer on a tiny corpus; extract nearest neighbors by cosine similarity and investigate a failure.
exercises.deliverables: embedding.py; neighbors.csv; 2D projection.png; notes.md on distributional meaning and limitations.

exercises.title: Translation and alignment
exercises.implementation:
Hand: write encoder/decoder tensor shapes and calculate one attention-weighted context vector.
Code: make a tiny sequence copy or word-translation task with nn.LSTM encoder/decoder and additive attention; save a token alignment heatmap.
exercises.deliverables: seq2seq_attention.py; notes.md (worked context); alignment.png; five input/output examples.

exercises.title: Attention matrix by hand
exercises.implementation:
Hand: compute all 3×3 QKᵀ/√d scores, softmax weights, weighted values, and a causal mask for three tokens.
Code: reproduce with NumPy, then check against PyTorch scaled_dot_product_attention; compare masked/unmasked outputs.
exercises.deliverables: notes.md (full matrix); attention_check.py; weights.csv; masked_vs_unmasked.png.

exercises.title: Compare pretraining objectives
exercises.implementation:
Hand: turn one short sentence into next-token, masked-token, and text-to-text training examples; list visible context for each.
Code: write dataset builders; train tiny PyTorch next-token and masked-token baselines on the same toy corpus (T5 objective as examples only).
exercises.deliverables: objectives.md; make_examples.py; examples.jsonl; train_small.py; loss_curves.png.
exercises.stack: PyTorch, Python; Hugging Face tokenizers optional

exercises.title: Three ways to make points
exercises.implementation:
Hand: write the VAE reconstruction/KL terms, GAN min–max roles, and one diffusion denoising step.
Code: use small PyTorch MLPs on a 2D two-moons mixture; train VAE, GAN, and diffusion toy models with identical data and seeds.
exercises.deliverables: generative_notes.md; three training scripts/notebook sections; samples.png; training_curves.png; comparison table.

exercises.title: Learn without labels
exercises.implementation:
Hand: calculate a small contrastive loss with one positive and two negatives; sketch patch masking.
Code: train a compact image encoder with two augmentations per image; freeze it and fit a linear probe. Compare to a random encoder; discuss MAE separately.
exercises.deliverables: self_supervised_notes.md; augmentations.png; encoder.py; probe_results.csv; neighbor_grid.png.

exercises.title: Images and text in one space
exercises.implementation:
Hand: compute cosine similarity for one image/text vector pair and explain zero-shot ranking.
Code: run pretrained CLIP on a small labeled image folder and candidate captions; store score matrix and inspect two mistakes.
exercises.deliverables: clip_retrieval.py; similarity.csv; ranked_examples.png; notes.md with failure analysis.

exercises.title: Compute budget trade-off
exercises.implementation:
Hand: calculate one log–log slope from three size/loss points and compare two equal-compute allocations.
Code: build an illustrative or measured table; fit simple curves and plot model size, token count, compute versus loss. Label toy findings clearly.
exercises.deliverables: scaling_notes.md (worked slope); scaling.py; measurements.csv; two plots; allocation comparison.

exercises.title: Preference pairs and DPO
exercises.implementation:
Hand: label five preference pairs; calculate one DPO log-sigmoid loss term from supplied policy/reference log-probabilities.
Code: implement that loss in PyTorch tensors and vary the preference strength β; do not fine-tune a large LLM here.
exercises.deliverables: preferences.csv; notes.md (worked loss); dpo_loss.py; beta_curve.png; reward-model versus DPO diagram.

exercises.title: Verifier-backed reasoning
exercises.implementation:
Hand: define an exact arithmetic verifier and grade two candidate reasoning traces; note what answer-only grading misses.
Code: generate 20 small tasks, run supplied or local-model responses through a Python verifier, compare prompt formats and record failure types.
exercises.deliverables: tasks.jsonl; verifier.py; eval_results.csv; notes.md with examples and limits of this toy study.

exercises.title: Retrieve before answering
exercises.implementation:
Hand: mark which passage supports an answer and identify one unsupported claim.
Code: index 10 short docs with TF-IDF, retrieve top-k, write cited answers from retrieved text; optional embedding retriever. No paid model API needed.
exercises.deliverables: docs/; retrieval.py; answers.jsonl with citations; retrieval_metrics.csv; failure_notes.md.

exercises.title: Low-rank update
exercises.implementation:
Hand: for W∈R^(d×k), derive full d·k parameters versus rank-r update r(d+k).
Code: freeze a PyTorch nn.Linear weight, train two low-rank factors, then compare with full fine-tuning on a small classification task.
exercises.deliverables: lora_notes.md; lora_layer.py; parameter_counts.csv; adaptation_curves.png.

exercises.title: Graph or audio branch
exercises.implementation:
Hand: choose one branch: calculate one normalized neighbor aggregation (graph) or a dilated causal receptive field (audio).
Code: graph—GCNConv on Karate Club; audio—small causal Conv1d predictor. State which branch you chose.
exercises.deliverables: notes.md; graph_gcn.py + node_plot.png OR audio_causal.py + waveform_plot.png; short results.csv.

exercises.title: Read protein-model outputs
exercises.implementation:
Hand: annotate a structure figure with sequence inputs, predicted coordinates, confidence, and AF2 versus AF3 scope.
Code: download a public PDB/mmCIF example; parse residues/coordinates and plot a simple distance map. No AlphaFold retraining.
exercises.deliverables: structure_notes.md; parse_structure.py; distance_map.png; source accession and validation caveats.

exercises.title: When to abstain
exercises.implementation:
Hand: score four correct/wrong/abstain examples under two explicit rules and predict how incentives change.
Code: create 20 answerable/unanswerable items; compute accuracy, coverage, and error rate at several confidence thresholds.
exercises.deliverables: scoring_notes.md; questions.csv; evaluate_abstention.py; accuracy_coverage.png; results.csv.

exercises.title: Negative sampling versus co-occurrence
exercises.implementation:
Prerequisites: E14.
Hand: calculate one positive/negative skip-gram loss and one weighted GloVe residual from a tiny co-occurrence table; distinguish the two objectives.
Code: build a small corpus and co-occurrence counts; train tiny skip-gram with negative sampling and GloVe objectives using NumPy or PyTorch. Inspect nearest neighbors within each model and record vocabulary, window, seeds and data limits; do not compare coordinates across independently trained spaces.
exercises.deliverables: notes.md; corpus.txt; word_objectives.py; neighbors.csv; loss_curves.png; model/data settings.

exercises.title: Dropout and overfitting
exercises.implementation:
Prerequisites: E02.
Hand: apply an inverted-dropout mask to a small activation vector and show why dividing retained activations by the keep probability preserves the expectation; state train/eval behavior.
Code: implement inverted dropout and compare it with PyTorch on fixed masks. Train a small MLP with and without dropout on the same fixed train/validation split, keeping model and budget constant; report multiple seeds and a case where dropout may not help.
exercises.deliverables: notes.md; dropout.py; train_mlp.py; metrics.csv; train_validation_curves.png; seed and split settings.

exercises.title: Batch versus layer normalization
exercises.implementation:
Prerequisites: E02.
Hand: for a small batch-by-feature matrix, mark the axes and calculate BatchNorm and LayerNorm means, variances and affine outputs; use biased variance for the normalization calculation.
Code: implement both normalizations in NumPy and compare with PyTorch BatchNorm1d and LayerNorm. Show BatchNorm train/eval and running-statistic behavior, including its running-variance convention; vary the other examples in a batch and test which outputs change. Keep epsilon, affine parameters and axes explicit.
exercises.deliverables: notes.md; normalization.py; normalization_checks.csv; batch_composition.csv; train_eval_comparison.md.

exercises.title: From REINFORCE to PPO
exercises.implementation:
Prerequisites: E11.
Hand: calculate a REINFORCE update for a categorical policy with an action-independent baseline; evaluate the PPO clipped surrogate for positive and negative advantages and several probability ratios.
Code: train REINFORCE on a tiny bandit, then implement and test PPO clipped loss on a fixed batch of actions, advantages and detached old log-probabilities. Plot clipping behavior and record sample/seed variability. A full on-policy PPO environment run is optional; this toy exercise does not reproduce RLHF.
exercises.deliverables: notes.md; reinforce_bandit.py; ppo_loss.py; bandit_rewards.csv; ppo_clipping.png; tests for both advantage signs.

exercises.title: Word2Vec, ELMo and BERT in context
exercises.implementation:
Prerequisites: E14, E15, E16, E17.
Hand: choose sentences using bank in financial and river contexts; explain why a static lookup is unchanged and calculate a learned softmax-weighted mixture of three toy ELMo layers, including the scale parameter.
Code: extract genuine pretrained Word2Vec, ELMo and BERT token vectors for the same marked word in at least four sentences (or use a documented cached export of those vectors). Compute cosine similarities separately within each model; record exact model/checkpoint, source, layer/mix, token alignment and subword pooling. Plot within-model same-sense versus different-sense comparisons. Never compare raw vectors across models. An optional small bidirectional LSTM is an ELMo-inspired demonstration, not a substitute for the three-model comparison or a full ELMo reproduction.
exercises.deliverables: notes.md; sentences.jsonl; compare_context.py; vectors.npz or reproducible extraction instructions; provenance.json; within_model_similarities.csv; context_comparison.png.
exercises.stack: Python, NumPy, Matplotlib; Transformers for BERT; original ELMo/Word2Vec tools or documented cached vectors in separate environments

exercises.title: Recurrent language-model transfer
exercises.implementation:
Prerequisites: E15, E17.
Hand: sketch language-model pretraining, target-domain adaptation and classifier fine-tuning; assign discriminative learning rates and a gradual-unfreezing schedule for a small recurrent classifier.
Code: pretrain a tiny LSTM next-token model on a small corpus, adapt it to unlabeled training-domain text, then compare a frozen encoder, gradual unfreezing and a classifier trained from scratch on fixed labeled splits. Keep validation/test text out of language-model fitting and report multiple seeds, data sizes and learning rates. Label this ULMFiT-inspired; it does not reproduce the full AWD-LSTM recipe.
exercises.deliverables: notes.md; train_language_model.py; finetune_classifier.py; splits.json; transfer_metrics.csv; learning_curves.png.

exercises.title: BERT and RoBERTa training ablations
exercises.implementation:
Prerequisites: E16, E17.
Hand: construct fixed and dynamically resampled masked-token examples; design a one-factor-at-a-time ablation table, including how to hold training tokens, updates and evaluation masks constant.
Code: extend the tiny masked LM from E17; compare fixed versus dynamic masks using the same architecture, corpus, optimizer, token budget and held-out evaluation. Use the same held-out mask set and several seeds; keep other recipe changes separate. Record the no-next-sentence-prediction choice. Label results as RoBERTa-inspired toy ablations, not a reproduction.
exercises.deliverables: notes.md; mask_examples.py; train_ablation.py; ablation_config.json; metrics.csv; heldout_loss.png.

tracks.teaches: Move from neurons and gradients to optimization, regularization and normalization.
Use baselines, search, and probabilistic reasoning.
Follow handwriting, image benchmarks, CNN training, residual networks and masks.
Connect value learning, policy gradients, planning and PPO to RLHF.
Study recurrence, alignment, layer normalization, attention and contextual representations.
Compare static and contextual vectors, recurrent and Transformer transfer, scaling and alignment; read prerequisites before linked exercises.
Compare generation procedures and image–text alignment.
Explore non-text structures and scientific prediction.

placements.reason: Read the original Word2Vec paper, its negative-sampling follow-up, then GloVe before contextual embeddings.
Establish dropout as a practical neural-network regularization technique.
Understand batch normalization before modern CNN training recipes.

placements.placement: Immediately before Attention Is All You Need.
placements.reason: Layer normalization is a component of the original Transformer.

placements.placement: After recurrence/attention foundations; before GPT and BERT.
placements.reason: ELMo and ULMFiT show contextual features and recurrent-model transfer; ELMo does not require Transformer architecture.
Use RoBERTa to examine which gains come from the pretraining recipe.

placements.placement: Before InstructGPT in the broad path; after Q-learning foundations in the RL path.
placements.reason: Read REINFORCE before PPO, then connect policy optimization to RLHF.

order_note: The broad sequence groups learning dependencies and topics, rather than sorting every paper by publication date. IDs stay fixed; follow the displayed order. Read all papers and prerequisites linked to an exercise before attempting it. Attention Is All You Need introduces the Transformer architecture used by BERT; ELMo uses bidirectional LSTMs.
